result.summary: The intersection is equipped with basic pedestrian infrastructure including marked zebra crosswalks, sidewalks, and signalized crossings. However, the environment lacks physical traffic calming measures such as curb extensions, leaving pedestrians exposed to traffic for the full width of the roadway.

hazards.name: Wide curb radius
hazards.description: The corner geometry allows for relatively high-speed vehicle turns, increasing risk to pedestrians at the crossing.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground left corner near the pedestrian

hazards.name: Unprotected crossing exposure
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross the entire width of the street and parking lanes without any physical refuge or curb extensions.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and slow down turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Refresh
interventions.description: Repaint the existing zebra markings with high-durability, high-visibility materials to improve driver awareness.

result.summary: The image shows a standard urban intersection with marked zebra crosswalks and sidewalks on both sides. While basic infrastructure is present, the wide roadway and lack of pedestrian refuge islands or curb extensions increase exposure for people crossing.

hazards.name: Sun Glare
hazards.description: Intense direct sunlight creates significant glare, likely blinding drivers and making it difficult to see pedestrians or traffic signals.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Exposure
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross the entire width of the roadway without a median or refuge island.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and improve sight lines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a raised island in the center of the roadway to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before vehicles get a green light.

result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility continental crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and wide sidewalks in a mixed-use commercial area. While basic infrastructure is present, the wide roadway and lack of permanent physical curb extensions or medians leave pedestrians exposed to traffic for a significant distance.

hazards.name: Wide turning radius
hazards.description: The corner geometry allows for relatively high-speed vehicle turns across the pedestrian path, despite the presence of flexible delineators.

hazards.name: Unprotected crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross the entire width of the roadway without a refuge island or physical curb extensions to shorten the exposure time.

interventions.title: Permanent Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Replace flexible delineators with concrete curb extensions to physically shorten the crossing distance and slow turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Raised Crosswalk
interventions.description: Elevate the crosswalk to the level of the sidewalk to act as a speed table and increase pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle green light.

result.summary: The image shows an urban intersection with a high-visibility continental crosswalk and a bike lane protected by flexible delineators. While basic pedestrian infrastructure like sidewalks and traffic signals are present, the wide roadway and parked vehicles near the crossing create potential visibility and exposure risks.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars on the right side of the street are positioned close to the crosswalk, potentially obscuring pedestrians from the view of oncoming drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway, adjacent to the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a mid-block refuge, increasing exposure to vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway at the marked crosswalk.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve sight lines between drivers and pedestrians.
